source.title: On the arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula for GSpin Shimura varieties

summary:
Li and Zhang formulate and prove a local arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport–Zink spaces, the orthogonal analogue of the unitary Kudla–Rapoport conjecture (Theorem 1.2.1). For F = Q_p (p odd) and every lattice L of rank n in the space V^ε_m of special quasi-endomorphisms (m = n + 1 ≥ 3, ε = ±1), Int^ε(L) = ∂Den^ε(L). By p-adic uniformization of Kisin's models this gives the semi-global formula at a good prime (Theorem 1.3.1).

The proof follows the unitary strategy along a rank n − 1 lattice L^♭. The new point is that W = (L^♭_F)^⊥ is two-dimensional, so the vertical parts have singularities when W is isotropic.
- **Horizontal side.** The horizontal part is a sum of primitive quasi-canonical and Gross–Keating cycles indexed by horizontal lattices (Theorem 5.3.1), and the horizontal identity reduces to Gross–Keating (Theorem 7.2.2).
- **Geometric vertical side.** The vertical part lives on the Deligne–Lusztig strata (Proposition 6.1.1, via specialization on a torus). The Tate conjecture for these strata (Theorem 6.3.2, via Lusztig) reduces it to Deligne–Lusztig curves, whose intersection function 1 − q, 1, 0 is Fourier self-dual up to γ_V = −1 (Theorem 7.4.1, Corollaries 7.5.3, 7.6.10).
- **Analytic vertical side.** New explicit formulas for orthogonal local densities in both ε cases (§3) and weighted counting identities (§8.2) give recurrences for the partial Fourier transform (Proposition 8.1.2).
- **Conclusion.** A classification of O(W)-invariant distributions via the SL₂ Weil representation and newforms (Proposition 9.1.3) gives the matching geometric recurrences (Proposition 9.2.3), and an induction on val(L^♭) concludes (Theorem 9.3.2).

The libraries have none of this. The atlas plans the local quadratic invariants (GN.2), Fourier analysis (AL.0) and the global Weil representation (MP.4).

Routes:
- the cycle theory and both arithmetic Siegel–Weil formulas to GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights, and the GSpin Rapoport–Zink spaces and integral models to OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake (both candidates of earlier extractions);
- sources: local densities to GN.3, the invariant-distribution classification to MP.3, and Tate's theorem to R07.1.

Seven source issues are recorded: five groups of misprints (one of them corrected in the final version), an edge case in which the simplified counting formulas of Lemmas 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 fail, and a gap in the argument of Remark 4.11.5 (the lift of an isometry to J(F) preserving the component N), which supplies the O(W)-invariance used in Lemma 9.2.2. The main identities were rechecked numerically where possible.

items.name: Theorem 1.2.1 = Theorem 4.15.1 (local arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula for GSpin Rapoport–Zink spaces)
items.statement: Let F = Q_p, p odd, m = n + 1 ≥ 3, ε ∈ {±1}, N = N^ε_n the connected GSpin Rapoport–Zink space attached to the self-dual lattice H^ε_m, and V = V^ε_m its space of special quasi-endomorphisms (χ(V) = ε, Hasse invariant −1). For every O_F-lattice L ⊆ V of rank n: Int^ε(L) = ∂Den^ε(L), where Int^ε(L) = χ(N, O_{Z(x_1)} ⊗^L ⋯ ⊗^L O_{Z(x_n)}) (1.2.0.1) and ∂Den^ε(L) = −(d/dX)|_{X=1}Den^ε(X, L), Den^ε(p^{−k}, L) = Den(H^ε_{m+2k}, L)/Den(H^ε_{m+2k}, H^ε_n), with Den^ε(X, L) = −X^{val(L)}Den^ε(1/X, L).
items.locator: §1.2, (1.2.0.1), Theorem 1.2.1, pp.2–4; Theorem 4.15.1, p.31; proof §9.3, pp.65–67, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: The orthogonal analogue of the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture; m = 4 was known (Gross–Keating/Wedhorn for ε = +1, Terstiege for ε = −1). Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.

items.name: Theorem 1.3.1 = Theorem 12.9.1 (semi-global arithmetic Siegel–Weil formula)
items.statement: For F = Q, V of signature (n − 1, 2) with m = n + 1 ≥ 3, p > 2 with K_p = GSpin(Λ_p) hyperspecial, V the incoherent positive definite nearby space, ϕ_K ∈ S(V^n_f) p-admissible (K-invariant, ϕ_{K,p} = 1_{(Λ_p)^n}) and T ∈ Sym_n(Q)_{>0}: Int_{T,p}(ϕ_K)q^T = c_K·∂Eis_{T,p}(z, ϕ_K), with q^T = ψ_∞(½ tr Tz) = e^{πi tr Tz} and c_K = (−1)^n/vol(K). Proof: p-adic uniformization reduces Int_{T,p} to Theorem 4.15.1 and Remark 3.4.9, the prime-to-p orbital integrals give Π_{v≠p,∞} W_{T,v}(1, 0, ϕ_{K,v}) [Kud97b, Prop. 1.2], and q^T = c_∞W_{T,∞} [BY21, Prop. 4.3(ii)]; the sign is γ^n_V = (−1)^n.
items.locator: Theorem 1.3.1, p.5; Theorem 12.9.1 and proof, pp.76–77, authors' final version (2 March 2022)
items.note: Remark 1.3.2: a global version (all T, all places) is harder for GSpin than for unitary groups (no split places, p = 2). Remark 1.3.3: F = Q_p is needed for [HP17, Kim18a]. Routed to the Part II GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), the candidate proposed by PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22.

items.name: Lemma 9.3.1 (reducing L^♭)
items.statement: For integral L^♭ of rank n − 1 with invariants (a_1, …, a_{n−1}) and x ∈ Ω(L^♭): (i) if x ∉ L^♭ ⊥ W^{≥a_{n−1}}, then L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with val(L′^♭) < val(L^♭) (Smith normal form of the fundamental matrix); (ii) if x ∈ L^♭ ⊥ W^{=a_{n−1}} and L^♭ is co-isotropic, then L^♭ + ⟨x⟩ = L′^♭ + ⟨x′⟩ with L′^♭ co-anisotropic and val(L′^♭) = val(L^♭).

items.name: Definition 4.6.1 and Proposition 4.10.1 (special cycles Z(L); special divisors are flat Cartier divisors)

items.name: Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_W, minuscule cycles V(Λ) and the Bruhat–Tits stratification (§§4.7–4.9)
items.statement: For the non-split quadratic space W of dimension 2(d + 1) over F_q, Y_W is a connected component of the locus in OGr_{d+1}(W) with dim(U + σ(U)) = d + 2, smooth projective of dimension d, stratified by generalized Deligne–Lusztig varieties X_{P_i}(w_i) with open stratum of Coxeter type [HP14, Prop. 3.8; HLZ19, Prop. 2.5.1] (Y_W ≅ P¹ for d = 1). For a vertex lattice Λ ⊆ V, t(Λ) is even with 2 ≤ t(Λ) ≤ t_max = m − 2, m − 1, m for (m even, ε = +1), m odd, (m even, ε = −1) (4.8.0.1) [HP17, 5.1.2], and V(Λ) = Z(Λ) (reduced [LZ18, Thm. B]) ≅ Y_{W_Λ,κ̄}, W_Λ = Λ^∨/Λ. N^red = ⋃ V(Λ), V(Λ) ⊆ V(Λ′) iff Λ ⊇ Λ′, V(Λ) ∩ V(Λ′) = V(Λ + Λ′) or ∅, strata V(Λ)° ≅ Y°_{W_Λ} [HP17, §6.5, Thm. D(iii)], and Z(L)^red = ⋃_{L ⊆ Λ} V(Λ) (4.9.0.2) [Soy17, Prop. 4.2].

items.name: Proposition 6.1.1, Remark 6.1.2 and Definition 6.2.1 (the vertical part lives on N^red)
items.statement: For L^♭ of rank n − 1, Z(L^♭)_V is supported on N^red: a formal curve through a unique closed point would specialize a non-basic isocrystal to a basic one, but its (L^♭_F)^⊥-component lies in B(T) for the torus T = SO(W), where specialization is trivial [RR96, §1.7, Thm. 3.6]. The torus argument also reproves [LZ, Lemma 5.1.1] (Remark 6.1.2).

items.name: Lemma 6.3.1 and Theorem 6.3.2 (the Tate conjecture for the Deligne–Lusztig varieties Y_d)
items.statement: For Y_d = Y_W (dim W = 2(d + 1), non-split) with strata X°_i and closures X_i: the Frobenius F = F_{q²} acts semisimply on H^{2j}(Y°_d)(j), H^{2j}(X°_i)(j), H^{2j}(Y_d − X_i)(j) with no invariants for j ≥ 1 ([Lus76, 7.3 case ²D_n, 6.1]); hence H^{2i}(Y_d)(i)^{F^s=1} is spanned by the classes of the irreducible components of X_{d−i} (the Tate conjecture holds for Y_d) and equals the generalized 1-eigenspace (as [LZ, Thm. 5.2.2]).

items.name: Theorem 7.4.1, Lemma 7.4.2, Remarks 7.4.3–7.4.4 and Corollaries 7.4.5–7.4.6 (intersections with Deligne–Lusztig curves)
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert⁴(V): Int_{V(Λ)}(x) = 1 − q for x ∈ Λ, 1 for x ∈ Λ^∨ \ Λ with val(x) ≥ 0, and 0 otherwise (reduction to V^−_4, where Z(x) ≅ Drinfeld's space for val(x) = 1, giving (q + 1) + (−2q)); I/I² ≅ O(2q) and the self-intersection of V(Λ) in N_κ̄ is −2q (Lemma 7.4.2, via the tangent sheaf O(2) ⊕ O(−2q) on M^HB [Ter11, KR99]); Int_{V(Λ)} = −q(1 + q)1_Λ + Σ_{Λ ⊂ Λ′ ∈ Vert²(V)} 1_{Λ′} (Corollary 7.4.5); Int_{L^♭,V} ∈ L¹_loc(Ω(L^♭)) extends to D(V), and to S(V) if L^♭ is co-anisotropic (Corollary 7.4.6). Remark 7.4.3: the same method gives 1 − q² in the unitary case of [LZ, Lemma 6.2.1]; Remark 7.4.4: −2q matches [TX19].

items.name: Lemma 7.5.1, Remark 7.5.2, Corollary 7.5.3 and §7.6 (local modularity: Int_{L^♭,V}^ = γ_V Int_{L^♭,V})
items.statement: For Λ ∈ Vert⁴(V), Int_{V(Λ)}^ = γ_V Int_{V(Λ)} with γ_V = −1 (Lemma 7.5.1; SL₂(O_F)-invariance under the Weil representation, Remark 7.5.2), hence Int_{L^♭,V}^ = γ_V Int_{L^♭,V} in D(V) (Corollary 7.5.3). For Λ of type 2d + 2: c_{1,V(Λ)}(x) = c_1(O(−Z(x))|_{V(Λ)}) and c_{V(Λ)} = c_1^d are Λ-invariant (Lemma 7.6.4); c_{1,V(Λ)}(x) = −(1 + q^{d+1})^{−1}Σ_{y ∈ W_Λ \ 0, (y,y)=0} c_{1,V(Λ)}(y) for x ∈ Λ (Lemma 7.6.5); c_{V(Λ)} = c(d)·(1 − q^d, 1, 0) with c(d) = Π_{i<d}(1 − q^i) (Lemma 7.6.6); c_{V(Λ)} = (c(d)/c′(d))Σ_{Λ′ ∈ Vert⁴, Λ′ ⊇ Λ} Int_{V(Λ′)}, c′(d) = Π_{i=2}^d(1 + q^{i+1}) (Lemma 7.6.7); hence ĉ_{V(Λ)} = γ_V c_{V(Λ)} (Corollary 7.6.8), K-theoretic local modularity (Theorem 7.6.9) and Int_{V(Λ)}^ = γ_V Int_{V(Λ)} for all types (Corollary 7.6.10), giving a proof of Corollary 7.5.3 without [Zha21, (B.3)] for formal schemes (Remark 7.6.11).

items.name: Definition 9.2.1, Lemma 9.2.2 and Proposition 9.2.3 (recurrences for the geometric partial Fourier transform)
items.statement: Int^⊥_{L^♭,V} ∈ L¹_loc(W^an) (in S(W) if L^♭ is co-anisotropic) lies in D(W)_k for some k: it is O(W)(F)-invariant (Remark 4.11.5 and Theorem 7.2.2), O_F^×-invariant, supported in W^{≥−k}, and its Fourier transform γ_V Int_{L^♭,V}|_W is supported on W° (Corollary 7.5.3). items.name: Theorem 9.3.2 (Int_{L^♭} = ∂Den_{L^♭} on Ω(L^♭)) and the proof of Theorem 4.15.1
items.statement: For L^♭ of rank n − 1, Int_{L^♭} = ∂Den_{L^♭} on Ω(L^♭). Proof: non-integral L^♭ gives 0 = 0; a_1 = 0 reduces to smaller n by the cancellation laws (4.14.0.4), (3.4.8.1); otherwise induct on val(L^♭): by Lemma 9.3.1 the difference is 1_{L^♭} ⊗ φ^⊥ with supp φ^⊥ ⊆ W^{≥a_{n−1}} (co-anisotropic) or W^{≥a_{n−1}+1} (co-isotropic, using the co-anisotropic case); the partial Fourier transforms of the vertical parts agree near W^{=−1} ∪ W^{=0} (∪ W^{=1}), and the recurrences of Propositions 8.1.2 and 9.2.3 propagate the vanishing. Theorem 4.15.1 follows by writing L = L^♭ + ⟨x⟩.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 4.11.5, p.30 (final version; also arXiv v1); used in the proof of Lemma 9.2.2 (i), p.64
sourceIssues.printed: "If L, L′ ⊆ V are isometric O_F-lattices of rank n, then we may find g ∈ SO(V)(F) such that L = gL′. We may further lift g to g̃ ∈ GSpin(V)(F) = J(F) such that η(g) = 1. Then the automorphism g̃ of N (see §4.4, 4.5) carries ^𝕃Z(L′) to ^𝕃Z(L). In particular, Int(L) only depends on the isometry class of L."
sourceIssues.correction: A lift g̃ ∈ J(F) of g ∈ SO(V)(F) has spinor norm η(g̃) = sn(g) in F^×/(F^×)², so η(g̃) = 1 forces sn(g) = 1. What the argument needs is only val η(g̃) = 0, since g̃ carries RZ^{(ℓ)}_G to RZ^{(ℓ + val η(g̃))}_G (§4.5) and N = RZ^{(0)}_G; that is available exactly when some isometry carrying L′ to L has spinor norm of even valuation, which the remark does not establish.
sourceIssues.reason: There are isometric pairs for which every isometry has spinor norm of odd valuation. Take m even and ε = −1: for m even and U unimodular, ϵ(ϖU) = χ(U), so V^−_m ≅ ϖ·H^−_{m,F}. Write H^−_m = M ⊥ ⟨w⟩ with M self-dual of rank n = m − 1, and let L ⊆ V be M with the scaled form, so that all its fundamental invariants are 1 and val(w) = 1. An element of SO(V)(F) stabilizing L preserves L_F and the line L^⊥_F, hence is a product of an even number of reflections in vectors of L or of L^⊥_F (for p odd the orthogonal group of a unimodular lattice is generated by the reflections in its vectors of unit norm, O'Meara 92:4); each such reflection has spinor norm of valuation 1, so the stabilizer has spinor norms of even valuation. Since V is isotropic, sn : SO(V)(F) → F^×/(F^×)² is surjective; choosing h with val sn(h) odd and L′ = hL gives isometric lattices such that every g ∈ SO(V)(F) with gL′ = L has val sn(g) odd. Remark 4.11.5 is the invariance input for Lemma 9.2.2 (i) (the O(W)(F)-invariance of Int^⊥_{L^♭,V}), hence for Proposition 9.2.3 and Theorem 9.3.2. The conclusion is presumably true — Theorem 4.15.1 asserts it, and for m = 4, ε = −1 it follows from Terstiege's explicit formulas (Remark 4.15.2) — and an automorphism of RZ_G outside J(F) shifting the components would supply it; but no such argument is given here, and this extraction did not settle it.
